title_en: Jilin Province Financial Holding Group Co., Ltd. v. Jilin Province Financial Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over company dissolution

full_text_en:
Jilin Province Financial Holding Group Co., Ltd. v. Jilin Province Financial Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over company dissolution

Ruling Summary

Where a major shareholder, taking advantage of its dominant position, makes unilateral decisions and, without authorization, lends company funds to its affiliated companies, thereby harming the rights and interests of minority shareholders, causing intensified shareholder conflicts, serious difficulties in the company's operational management, and failure to achieve the business purpose, and where the issue cannot be resolved through other means, the people's court shall support the minority shareholder's petition for dissolution of the company.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 1474

Reapplying Petitioner (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Jilin Province Financial Asset Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 2034, East Auxiliary Building, Entrepreneurship Service Center Building, No. 6666 Jingyue Ecological Development Street, Jingyue District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Baojun, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaojian, Attorney at Beijing Tiantong (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Reapplying Petitioner (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Building 41, Jinhu Road, Longgang District, Huludao City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xinjian, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Cao Lin, Attorney at Beijing Tiantong (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhuang, Attorney at Beijing Tiantong (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jilin Province Financial Holding Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 10606 Renmin Street, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Li Laihua, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zeng Qinghua, Attorney at Jilin Gongcheng Law Firm.

The reapplying petitioners, Jilin Province Financial Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Financial Management Company) and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongyun Group Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2018) Ji Min Zhong No. 619 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court in the case of company dissolution dispute with the respondent Jilin Province Financial Holding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Financial Holding Company), applied to this Court for a retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct a review, and the review has now been concluded.

Financial Management Company and Hongyun Group Company applied for a retrial pursuant to Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The main facts and grounds are as follows: (1) The shareholders' meeting and board of directors of Financial Management Company can be lawfully convened and form effective resolutions, and there is no situation of serious difficulty in operational management at the level of corporate governance. The judgment of first instance found that the corporate governance mechanism had failed and dissolved the company on that basis, which was erroneous in both fact-finding and application of law. A. Financial Management Company was able to and did implement the convocation, holding, and voting of the shareholders' meeting and board of directors. There is no fact in this case that the company was unable to form an effective shareholders' meeting resolution for two consecutive years. B. This case does not meet the statutory grounds for judicial dissolution of a company as specified in Items (1), (2), and (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II). There is no fact that Financial Management Company was unable to convene a shareholders' meeting or unable to form a shareholders' meeting resolution for two consecutive years; based on the company's equity ratio and the rules of procedure for shareholders' meetings, Financial Management Company is at any time capable of convening a shareholders' meeting and forming an effective resolution; the fact that directors appointed by Financial Holding Company refused to attend board meetings after the lawsuit was filed should not be considered as a factual factor in assessing whether the corporate governance structure is operating effectively. Therefore, there is no board deadlock that would warrant a mandatory dissolution of the company. (2) The judgment of first instance found that Financial Management Company, without shareholder consultation, lent a large amount of funds to affiliated companies of Hongyun Group Company, resulting in serious difficulties in operational management. This finding is inconsistent with the facts and should be corrected. The provision of loans by Financial Management Company to the affiliated companies of Hongyun Group Company was the common intention of both shareholders, and the lending did not cause actual losses to Financial Management Company, nor did it result in the inability to carry out the company's business. (3) Financial Management Company has continuously carried out its main business, and the development status of the main business does not constitute a statutory reason for judicial dissolution of the company. The judgment of second instance found that "departing from the company's purpose of establishment" constitutes "serious difficulties in operational management" within the meaning of judicial dissolution of a company, which is erroneous in both fact-finding and application of law and should be corrected. A. Financial Management Company has been committed to carrying out the business of acquiring and disposing of non-performing assets, but the results were not satisfactory due to objective constraints. The judgment of first instance found that it had never carried out the business of bulk acquisition and disposal of non-performing assets, which is inconsistent with the facts. B. According to publicly available data, the operations of other local asset management companies in China during the same period were also unsatisfactory. C. Both judgments of the original instanced found that conduct "departing from the company's purpose of establishment" met the conditions for judicial dissolution of a company for "serious difficulties in operational management," which is an error in the application of law. D. Even if Financial Management Company engaged in conduct "departing from the company's purpose of establishment," Financial Holding Company could have taken reasonable remedies such as proposing company dissolution, requesting the company to repurchase equity, reducing registered capital, or transferring equity, but it did not exercise these rights. (4) In terms of communication between shareholders, the basis of personal trust has not been lost. Without government intervention, Financial Management Company has not fallen into a company deadlock within the meaning of judicial dissolution. (5) In the reasoning of the judgment of second instance, the statement that "Financial Holding Company could not make such a choice (selling equity)" clearly contains local protectionism and has no factual or legal basis.

Financial Holding Company responded in its defense: The judgments of first and second instance were clear in fact-finding and correct in the application of law, and it requests the rejection of the retrial applications of the two reapplying petitioners. The main facts and grounds are as follows: (1) Hongyun Group Company abused its dominant position as a major shareholder to suppress and exclude Financial Holding Company from participating in business decision-making, manipulated Financial Management Company to unilaterally decide on major business matters, causing the company's operational decision-making mechanism to fail, deviating from the purpose of establishment, and resulting in serious difficulties in operational management. Continued existence would cause serious harm to the shareholders' interests. In this regard, the Jilin Provincial Financial Office issued a letter to perform its financial regulatory duties, promoting Financial Management Company to recover funds and return to its main business. (2) The operational decision-making mechanism of Financial Management Company has failed, the basis of personal trust has been lost, and the problem cannot be resolved through other means. Hongyun Group Company abused its dominant position as a major shareholder, long-term sidelined the company's shareholders' meeting and board of directors, and unauthorized misappropriation of more than 95% of the registered capital without repayment, intensifying conflicts between the parties. Since the end of 2016, the parties had begun negotiations on equity, but ultimately found no other solution. Financial Management Company also ceased all business activities from 2017, with original employees leaving one after another, the business premises being reclaimed, and the company effectively disintegrated. Continued existence would cause significant harm. (3) The conditions for company dissolution under Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China should not be limited to the several circumstances specified in Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II). Whether the conditions for company dissolution are met should be analyzed comprehensively based on the operational status of the company's organizational structure. Moreover, after the original court presided over the proceedings, all internal and external remedies have been exhausted, and no practical and feasible solution exists.

This Court holds that the core dispute among the parties in this case is whether Financial Management Company meets the conditions for judicial dissolution. The focal issues for review are: whether the operational management of Financial Management Company has encountered serious difficulties, and whether continued existence will cause significant harm to the shareholders' interests; and whether the company's difficulties can be resolved through other means.

I. Whether the operational management has encountered serious difficulties and whether continued existence will cause significant harm to the shareholders' interests

The relevant laws and judicial interpretations have clearly defined the circumstances under which serious difficulties in operational management may give rise to a petition for judicial dissolution. Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a company encounters serious difficulties in its operational management, the continued existence of which will cause significant harm to the interests of its shareholders, and the difficulties cannot be resolved through other means, shareholders holding 10% or more of the voting rights of all shareholders of the company may petition the people's court for dissolution of the company. Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II) provides that a shareholder who brings an action for dissolution of a company on any of the following grounds, and meets the requirements of Article 182 of the Company Law, shall be accepted by the people's court: (1) the company has been unable to convene a shareholders' meeting or general meeting for two consecutive years or more, resulting in serious difficulties in operational management; (2) the shareholders are unable to reach the statutory or quorum required by the company's articles of association when voting, and have been unable to form an effective resolution of the shareholders' meeting or general meeting for two consecutive years or more, resulting in serious difficulties in operational management; (3) there is a long-standing conflict among the directors of the company, and the conflict cannot be resolved through the shareholders' meeting or general meeting, resulting in serious difficulties in operational management; (4) there are other serious difficulties in operational management, and the continued existence of the company would cause significant harm to the interests of the shareholders. In this case, whether the operational management of Financial Management Company has encountered serious difficulties and whether it should be judicially dissolved shall be determined based on these provisions. Based on the facts found in the judgments of first and second instance, this Court is of the opinion that the judgments of first and second instance correctly found that Financial Management Company's operational management had encountered serious difficulties meeting the conditions for judicial dissolution.

First, from the perspective of the company's operations. Financial Management Company, as the only local asset management company in Jilin Province approved by the Jilin Provincial People's Government, had its main business as the bulk acquisition and disposal of non-performing assets, with the aim of preventing and mitigating local financial risks. However, shortly after its establishment, without the deliberation and decision of the shareholders' meeting or board of directors, Hongyun Group Company, by virtue of its control over Financial Management Company, unilaterally lent 965 million yuan out of the 1 billion yuan registered capital to its actually controlled affiliates Hongyun Investment Holding Co., Ltd., Liaoning Football Club Co., Ltd., and Hongyun Commercial Group Co., Ltd. This was the trigger for the subsequent conflicts between shareholders and the subsequent loss of personal trust within the company. Although Financial Holding Company and the Jilin Provincial Financial Supervision Department repeatedly urged Hongyun Group Company to resolve the loan issue and ensure the company's return to its main business, and Hongyun Group Company promised to recover the lent funds by the end of 2015 at the latest, as of December 31, 2016, the loan issue had not been resolved, and the company's bank deposit balance was only 2,686,465.85 yuan. Because the operating funds of Financial Management Company had been unilaterally diverted by Hongyun Group Company for loans that could not be recovered over a long period, the company's main business of bulk acquisition and disposal of non-performing assets could not be carried out normally, frustrating the purpose of the company's establishment and causing serious operational difficulties.

Second, from the perspective of the operation of the company's management mechanism. After its establishment on February 28, 2015, Financial Management Company did not convene annual shareholders' meetings or regular board of directors meetings as required by the company's articles of association, except for a board meeting held on April 27, 2015. The shareholders' meeting and board of directors meeting held on December 18, 2015, were temporary meetings convened after differences had arisen between the two shareholder parties. Thereafter, until Financial Holding Company filed this lawsuit in October 2017, although conflicts had emerged between the shareholder parties and the company's operations had encountered serious difficulties, Financial Management Company failed to convene shareholders' meetings or board of directors meetings to properly negotiate and resolve the existing problems. After Financial Holding Company filed this lawsuit, Financial Management Company successively convened a board of directors meeting and a shareholders' meeting in November 2017, but the number of directors in attendance did not meet the quorum required by the articles of association for convening a board meeting, and only Hongyun Group Company alone attended the shareholders' meeting. Financial Holding Company completely denied the legality of the convening procedures and the validity of the resolutions of these shareholders' meeting and board of directors meeting. Moreover, the fact that the shareholder parties had already resorted to litigation demonstrates that the conflicts between shareholders and between directors had intensified and could not be resolved by themselves, and the mechanisms of the shareholders' meeting and board of directors could no longer operate normally and function effectively. Under such circumstances, continuing to maintain the company's existence and the abnormal functioning of the shareholders' meeting would only result in the major shareholder, by taking advantage of its dominant position, making unilateral decisions that oppress and harm the interests of the other minority shareholder.

II. Whether the company's difficulties can be resolved through other means

After the conflict between Financial Holding Company and Hongyun Group Company arose over the lending of funds, the parties began to seek a resolution as early as 2015, but the issue remained unresolved until the filing of this lawsuit, and the basis of trust and cooperation between the shareholders gradually eroded. During this period, the parties also communicated multiple times regarding equity restructuring, but never reached an agreement on equity transfer. During the litigation of this case, the court of first instance, over a period of nearly ten months, repeatedly organized mediation between the parties, attempting to resolve the dispute through various means such as equity transfer, capital increase, and transfer of corporate control, but neither shareholder party accepted the other's mediation proposal, and ultimately no mediation agreement was reached. Under the circumstances where all means other than judicial dissolution had been exhausted without resolution, the courts of first and second instance correctly decided to dissolve Financial Management Company, both in law and in reason.

In conclusion, the retrial applications of Financial Management Company and Hongyun Group Company do not satisfy the circumstances specified in Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Paragraph 2 of Article 395 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The retrial applications of Jilin Province Financial Asset Management Co., Ltd. and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Wang Fubo
Judge: Song Chunyu
Judge: Yu Xiaohan
